clue.text: An area over which you can see ice contract? Wrong!

definitions.text: An area over which you can see ice contract? Wrong!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer asks whether a sea where pack ice shrinks is the place meant, then dismisses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the letters of AN, A and ICE CONTRACT rearrange into a southern sea where ice is visible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southern sea surrounding the polar continent is covered by pack ice, so ice is seen over it.

clue.text: Like a self-sufficient life?

parts.note: surface reading: describing a life lived independently, growing your own food
setter's reading: a life story that its subject wrote alone, needing no other biographer

explanation.walkthrough: Self-sufficiency suggests the good life of keeping goats, but here it means a life written by the self.
explanation.definitionFit: A memoir composed by its own subject is self-written, which is what the Greek roots of the adjective mean.

clue.text: Took steps of which one's said to be incapable

definitions.text: Took steps of which one's said to be incapable

parts.words: Took steps of which one's said to be incapable
parts.note: surface reading: someone acted in a way thought beyond them
setter's reading: the saying goes that it takes two to do this Latin dance, so one alone cannot

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'it takes two to tango' means a single person can't do this dance, so 'steps' are literal dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Performed the Argentine ballroom dance, a past-tense verb matching 'took steps'.

clue.text: Modified opinion about artist is received in shock

indicators.note: what is received in something is taken inside it, so one part goes within another

parts.note: RE means concerning, as in a letter heading
to appal is to shock or horrify
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders their view after learning, with alarm, that a painter has been welcomed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; 'shock' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh assessment that changes one's earlier view is a revised judgement, so the noun fits.

clue.text: The chap taken in by politician's proposition

indicators.note: someone taken in by another is held within them, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician; the 's is read as 'is'
the chap is 'he'

explanation.surface: A man is duped by a politician's offer or suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party; 'taken in' looks like 'fooled' but means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposed explanation or hypothesis put forward for argument is a supposition, a sense of proposition.

clue.text: Medicinal plant — measure after cold a medic's provided

indicators.note: one thing coming after another fixes their order, so this piece goes at the end

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
taken as written
MO is a medical officer; the 's is 'has'
a mile is a measure of distance

explanation.surface: A doctor with a chill has supplied a herbal remedy, given after some measured dose.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy-like herb is used for soothing tea and ointments, so it is a healing plant.

clue.text: It's clued oddly, as result of some rumination

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A setter admits a clue is strange, the product of chewing things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumination' looks like thinking hard, but it is literal chewing by cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and sheep regurgitate partly digested food to chew again; ruminating is that chewing.

clue.text: A colleague said you are not professional

parts.note: taken as written
a mate is a workmate or companion

indicators.note: said tells us to use how the words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: the two letters spoken sound like these words, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: A workmate remarks that you are no pro.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid enthusiast, or someone unskilled, is the opposite of a professional.

clue.text: Nevertheless, odd sects will include expert source for idea

parts.note: though can mean nevertheless, at the end of a sentence

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: Despite everything, eccentric religious groups will take in an expert, a source of new ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' reads as describing the sects, but it is the signal to rearrange them before the expert goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas arise from a sequence of mental reasoning steps, so that reasoning is where an idea comes from.

clue.text: Metal products contributing in fact in war effort

indicators.note: the words that are contributing supply the letters from within themselves, spanning a gap

parts.note: running across the end of fact, the whole of in and war, and the start of effort

explanation.surface: Factories turning out metal goods helped the war effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Household goods made of tin-plated iron are metal manufactured items.

clue.text: Following male doctor but had treatment in spa

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the next piece is placed behind the first

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the next words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: After a male doctor, someone else was also treated at a health resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun beside 'male', but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaking in warm mineral mud is a classic remedy offered at health resorts.

clue.text: Job, for example, not finished, so express disapproval

indicators.note: a thing not finished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A piece of work left incomplete earns jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like a task, but it is the biblical figure whose story is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting a derisive sound at a performer is a way of showing displeasure.

clue.text: Trunk left on board by ship's officer, containing new gold

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the officer

parts.note: a mate is a merchant ship's officer
N is the abbreviation for new
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A ship's officer leaves a chest aboard, holding freshly acquired gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left-hand side of a ship facing forward; Au is from Latin aurum.
explanation.definitionFit: A large travelling case opening into two halves is a type of luggage chest.

clue.text: Weird thing I spotted in swamp, very frightening

indicators.note: weird means strange or distorted, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is located inside it, so one letter sits within

parts.note: a marsh is a swamp
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange creature seen in a bog is truly terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like a bad dream is terrifying, so the adjective means extremely scary.

clue.text: Suffering losses up front, sold what is no longer fresh

indicators.note: losing at the front means each of the words drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, then headless
taken as written, then headless

explanation.surface: A trader making losses has sold goods past their best.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something stale, dated or overfamiliar, no longer novel.

clue.text: Old soldier's back cutting tree, one of small group at top

definitions.text: one of small group at top

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it, splitting it apart

parts.note: the larch is a conifer

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran's back is injured felling a tree; meanwhile one elite ruler looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchy is rule by a few, so a member of that powerful elite fits the definition.

clue.text: Enclosures for children from song writer, in addition to letter

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following one

parts.note: a postscript is something added to a letter
a pen is a writing tool
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: Playground pens are borrowed from a songwriter who also sends a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in addition to' reads as 'as well as', but 'in' is the insertion signal and 'addition to letter' is a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable fenced areas where toddlers play safely are pens for small children.

clue.text: Judges holding great power left negative decisions

indicators.note: to hold is to keep inside, so the other pieces go within the judges

parts.note: refs are referees, judges in sport
the USA is a superpower
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Sporting officials with great authority have left a string of rejections.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to requests produces rejections, and these are decisions that are negative.

clue.text: Proclaimed end of Northern race

indicators.note: something proclaimed is announced out loud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: the end of something is its finish

explanation.surface: An announcement declares a northern race over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a contest, which suits 'end', but here it is a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Finns are a Nordic people, so an adjective describing them describes that northern nation.

clue.text: Come forward with this neat clue, ultimately, by young setter

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word it governs

parts.note: the last letters of these three words
a setter is a dog breed, and a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: A beginner crossword setter is invited forward on the strength of a tidy clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer or present oneself is to move forward, the phrasal verb's everyday sense.

clue.text: Illustrations covering one form of exercise

indicators.note: to cover something is to surround it, so one goes within the other

parts.note: plates are full-page illustrations in a book
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pictures in a manual demonstrate a single type of workout.
explanation.definitionFit: The core-strengthening system devised by Joseph Pilates is a well-known fitness regime.

clue.text: Sound of composer for his fellow citizen

indicators.note: the sound of a name means its pronunciation, so we want a word spoken the same way

parts.note: Benjamin Britten was an English composer

explanation.surface: A composer's music speaks for his compatriots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back to the English composer, so a fellow citizen of his is someone from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten was British, so a compatriot of his is a native of Britain.

clue.text: It's adjacent to goal in which a player gets entangled with a net

indicators.note: things entangled are mixed up together, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer ends up tangled in the goal netting next to the posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints the goalmouth itself, which is where the answer lies.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football pitch the marked box in front of each goal is where fouls bring spot-kicks.

clue.text: Pope, Cleopatra and Napoleon have it in common

indicators.note: what the names have in common is a string of letters sitting inside each of them

parts.note: letters two to four of this name; the emperor's name holds the same three letters at its end

explanation.surface: A quiz question asks what links a pontiff, an Egyptian queen and a French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen popes have taken this papal name, including Leo the Great.

clue.text: Copy — trim it at end? Trim at both ends

indicators.note: trimming both ends cuts letters off the front and the back of the phrase, leaving its middle

parts.note: the middle of this phrase, once its first two and last two letters are cut

explanation.surface: Hairdressing advice: to copy a style, trim the ends, then trim both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Trim' is the instruction applied to the first phrase; the question mark marks the first half as a puzzle, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce, a direct synonym of the verb copy.

clue.text: A short distance behind at sea

parts.note: taken as written
ft is the abbreviation for foot, a short distance

explanation.surface: A boat trails slightly behind on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for the stern direction of a vessel, towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: National emblem that blows down when it's windy

definitions.text: National emblem that blows down when it's windy

parts.note: surface reading: a symbol knocked over by the wind
setter's reading: a plant whose fluffy seed heads, called its down, are blown by the wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows down' suggests falling over; read instead as the plant blowing its down, the feathery seeds. The plant is Scotland's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly purple-flowered plant is Scotland's national symbol, and its seeds have a fluffy down.

clue.text: The posy this son arranged, showing what plants can do

indicators.note: arranged suggests put into a new order, like flowers in a vase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy has arranged a bunch of flowers, showing a talent with plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Green plants make sugars from light, water and carbon dioxide; that process is their characteristic ability.
